Hi there—thank you for making time today. I’m Dr. Maya Bennett, a perinatal-mental-health clinician who works with new mothers. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a brief, well-studied questionnaire that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically during the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve. Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space. I’ll ask 10 questions; just answer in your own words—there are no right or wrong replies.

To start: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?

Honestly? It’s been kind of hard. My husband made a goofy face at the baby yesterday and normally I’d have laughed, but I just managed a weak smile. Most of the time things that used to crack me up feel flat, like I know they’re funny but the laughter doesn’t quite reach me.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… maybe once or twice I’ve managed a quick chuckle, but it feels forced. Mostly I just feel heavy, like I’m watching life happen from behind a pane of glass.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much anymore. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk around the neighborhood—but now even the stuff I know I *should* look forward to feels like a chore. I still go through the motions, but the spark isn’t really there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right—maybe I ate the wrong thing, or I’m not holding him the way he needs. When he wouldn’t nap yesterday I caught myself thinking, “I’m already failing him,” even though rationally I know babies just cry. The guilt sits in my chest like a weight.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart starts racing because I’m sure he’s going to choke, even though he’s latched fine. Or I’ll lie down and picture the bassinet tipping over for no reason. I know the fears aren’t logical, but I can’t switch them off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a couple of nights this week I woke up suddenly and my heart was pounding like something awful had happened, but the house was quiet and the baby was asleep. I couldn’t shake the feeling that something terrible was just about to happen, even though nothing was wrong.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes. Most days feel like I’m barely treading water. Between feedings, diapers, trying to sleep, and the racing thoughts, I keep thinking, “I can’t do this,” even though I’m still doing it. I haven’t broken down completely, but it’s like one more small thing—spit-up on a fresh shirt, a missed nap—could tip me over.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening almost every night this week. I lie down exhausted, but my mind just keeps spinning—mostly worries about the baby, replaying every little thing I did wrong during the day. It takes me over an hour to fall asleep, and then I wake up at two or three in the morning with my heart racing, so I end up staring at the ceiling until dawn.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud that follows me around. I still get up and do what I have to do for the baby, but I feel empty or like I’m on the verge of tears most of the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, I’ve cried twice this week—once in the shower on Tuesday and then yesterday when the baby wouldn’t settle. It’s never for long, just these sudden waves where the sadness feels too big to hold in, so the tears come for a minute or two and then I wipe my face and keep going.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

It has crossed my mind… maybe once or twice in the past week. Nothing planned—just a fleeting picture of “what if I wasn’t here,” especially when I’m feeling overwhelmed at 3 a.m. and can’t get back to sleep. I haven’t told anyone, and I don’t intend to act on it, but the thought did show up.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Symptom Highlights  
- Marked anhedonia, pervasive low mood, daily crying episodes  
- Sleep-onset and middle insomnia linked to ruminative guilt, “racing heart”  
- Excessive self-blame re: infant care; feels “failing him”  
- Near-daily free-floating anxiety, nocturnal panic attacks, intrusive catastrophic images  
- Endorses feeling “on edge,” overwhelmed, “treading water”  
- Passive, non-specific self-harm ideation (no plan/intent)  

Pattern / Risk Indicators  
Consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive and anxiety symptoms; safety concern flagged for presence of self-harm thoughts and prominent guilt.  

Screening Impression  
High index of suspicion for major postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; immediate safety assessment and follow-up evaluation recommended.
